explanation:
[EFFECT]
At low wind speeds (roughly below 17 km/h), windspeed has a negligible or very slightly positive effect on predicted bike demand. Once wind speeds climb above that threshold, the effect turns increasingly negative — the model predicts fewer rentals as winds get stronger. The steepest drop occurs at the highest wind speeds recorded (above ~30 km/h), where the contribution can reduce predicted demand by around 30–40%.

[IMPORTANCE]
Windspeed is the second-least important feature in the model, ranking 8th out of 9 features. Its overall influence on demand is modest compared to factors like hour of day or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION]
When strong winds are forecast (above roughly 30 km/h), the system can expect meaningfully lower rental activity, so operators could plan for reduced bike rebalancing needs and potentially scale back staffing at those times.
